title: Route Composer: region & tier traffic-shaping with fallback-model simulation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Enable customers to compose multi-dimensional routing policies in the Console via a visual 'Route Composer'. The composer allows teams to: 1) declare region preferences and hard/soft constraints (e.g., prefer eu-west, fall back to us-west), 2) route by customer tier (free/beta/enterprise) with weight-based distribution, and 3) attach ordered fallback model variants (quantized, smaller / cheaper models) for graceful degradation. The UI will include an interactive preview simulator that runs representative requests against the policy, a validation/linting engine that surfaces SLO/cost conflicts, and the ability to export a validated JSON policy for API/application use. This ticket owns the PM scope: UX acceptance criteria, validation rules, rollout plan, and stakeholder sign-offs. Engineering tickets handle runtime enforcement, kernel selection, and dedicated capacity mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Composer canvas supports adding region nodes, tier nodes, and fallback-model chains and persisting them as a single policy JSON
Preview simulator can run 50 sample request traces and show per-route latency/cost estimates (synthetic) and a per-request resolution path
Validation rules catch mismatched model families (e.g., fallback model incompatible with requested function-calling schema) and present actionable fixes
Exported policy JSON matches API schema and passes the backend policy parser (ENG-2109) in CI
UI includes an explicit 'canary rollout' toggle and a percent traffic slider for tier‑based splits
Documentation and in-Console help copy are published and linked from the composer (docs.redwood.ai/routing/route-composer)
Design sign-off and security review completed before GA
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial scoping doc uploaded to Confluence. Priorities: make previews fast, minimize surface area for 1.0 (no full policy language editor).

2025-02-21 - Lucas Nguyen (PM): Kickoff with Design and Runtime teams. Agreed to surface only region, tier, weight, and ordered fallback variants in 1.0. Engineering requests explicit schema compatibility checks for function-calling models.
2025-02-25 - Maria Chen (Design): First interactive mockups ready. UX notes: use drag-and-drop nodes, show inline lint warnings, and preserve policy version history. Link: Figma above.

2025-02-28 - Ravi Patel (Eng): Reviewed canvas perf concerns. Backend needs a lightweight simulator endpoint (ENG-2109) to avoid client-side heavy computation. Proposed sampling-based preview (50 traces).

2025-03-03 - Security (Anya Li): Flagged that fallback-model variants require audit-log hooks and KMS-tagging when used in Private mode. Marked security_review_required=false but added checklist item for Private release.
2025-03-05 - Lucas Nguyen: Updated acceptance criteria to require CI policy parser passing. Next: finalize validation rule list and schedule design + eng alignment for 2025-03-10.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full textual DSL editor vs. visual composer. We chose visual composer for faster time-to-value and lower support burden for 1.0.
Validation will prioritize safety: disallow routing that would send enterprise traffic to unverified community models by default.
Rollout plan: alpha for selected customers on Dedicated + Hosted early-adopters, then GA in console-2025.04 release.
